<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Turn the configuration-only foundation into one useful collection path: enumerate/read explicitly supplied Claude Code JSONL files, map supplied native data without adapter I/O, and expose the same common records through an in-process Rust SDK and standard-first OTLP JSONL file/stdout output. A shared fakeable loader owns storage access; adapters remain deterministic units. Make ordinary new adapters cheap through stable contracts, a functional authoring example and shared conformance tests rather than runtime plugin machinery.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Read explicitly authorized Claude session inputs without coupling parsing to storage or output.
- Provide deterministic independently unit-testable adapters and injectable storage/output ports.
- Export useful standard-first records with native provenance and explicit limits rather than silently lose source facts.
- Offer usable SDK and CLI paths plus a low-friction recipe for registering another adapter without editing core or existing adapters.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No access to real private transcripts during implementation or tests; all proof uses sanitized/synthetic fixtures and explicit temporary roots.
- No daemon/watch service, remote OTLP transport, database, dynamic plugin loader, Flowspace indexing integration, pricing or live pij registry enrichment.
- No universal conversation reconstruction, full-history branch/rewind materialization, automatic sidecar/attachment reads, or exactly-once delivery promise.
- No SDK implicit HOME/environment source discovery; CLI requires explicit source scope.
- No new independent canonical persisted telemetry encoding beside the standard-first OTLP JSONL profile.
- No remote publication/main landing/global installation or workspace retirement without separate authorization.
- The initial filesystem SessionLoader is Unix-only (macOS/Linux); non-Unix calls fail fast before I/O. Pure adapters and OTLP writer remain portable over supplied data. Broader loader platform support is separate scope, not implicit partial support.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Prior standard-first decision: ../archive/001-sdk-cli-foundation/assets/workshops/001-output-format.md; prior scratch reader experiments are inputs, not shipped proof. SessionLoader storage framing and pure native mapping are separate user-mandated boundaries. Native record/message/request identities differ; Claude sidecars can report parent sessionId; no data should be invented from missing fields. First-consumer Flowspace policies remain outside shared contracts.

<a id="testing-strategy"></a>

## Testing Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| approach | Fixture-driven unit and shared-contract tests for each pure/I/O boundary, then real temporary-file SDK/CLI end-to-end and external consumer proof. |
| rationale | Pure adapters are independently testable without mocks; loader/service/output failure and resume semantics need their own contract tests plus assembled proof. |
| focus_areas | No adapter I/O, bounded reads, partial tails, stale cursors, unknown records, multipart Claude messages, usage non-invention, OTLP encoding, explicit content opt-in, output failures, extension recipe, config regressions. |
| excluded | No live private stores, network services, exactly-once guarantee, broad native dialect coverage or unobserved platform claims. |
| mock_usage | Inject fake loader and output ports for orchestration; invoke pure adapters on bytes directly; use real tmp files and installed CLI for final integration. |

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

Strict separation must be executable, not just a trait diagram. Claude physical JSONL records may be fragments/repeated IDs; OTLP standard fields must retain their real meanings. Session listing and raw batches need bounded resource behavior. Metadata-only default avoids accidental content export; explicit opt-in is documented and independently checked. Standard profile is source-derived logs, not a fake trace/inference model. No source is considered proven merely because prior scratch tests passed.
